Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Detroit/Pontiac MI
645 AM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Seasonable temperatures today into Saturday with prevailing dry 
weather apart from a slight chance for a brief shower this afternoon 
or evening.

- A warming trend sends temperatures above normal early next week 
with increasing chances for showers and storms.

&&

.AVIATION...

Increasing surface high pressure and isentropic downglide will lead 
to quiet weather over much of Southeast Michigan.today. Lingering 
surface moisture is expected to result in a decent amount of 
boundary layer cumulus today with daytime heating. The increasing 
surface high pressure will also lead to a developing/organizing 
backdoor cold front feature off of Lake Huron by late afternoon and 
evening. Isolated shower activity will be possible along this 
boundary particularly near the Lake Huron shoreline. Cooling 
temperatures tonight with peak climo evapotranspiration will bring 
the potential for some fog at daybreak Friday morning, however, 
enough north gradient wind is anticipated to limit development.

D21/DTW Convection...No convection is forecast through the TAF 
period.

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* None.

&&

.PREV DISCUSSION...
Issued at 342 AM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

DISCUSSION...

A longwave trough is situated over the Great Lakes this morning with 
an embedded midlevel shortwave exiting toward Lake Ontario. At the 
surface, the cold front that passed through last night is now midway 
across Lake Erie. Thermal change behind this front is relatively 
weak, and guidance supports another seasonable day with highs near 
80. Diurnal instability will be stifled by mid-level warming via 
post-wave subsidence, but enough low-level moisture will exist for a 
healthy flare-up of cumulus. A few shallow late afternoon and 
evening showers will also be possible, mainly over the Thumb where 
veering northerly flow off the lake provides some convergence to act 
as a trigger.

A backdoor cold front marking a much drier air mass will arrive this 
evening and precede high pressure that settles in on Friday. Light 
northerly wind allows dew points to settle into the 50s, offering 
very pleasant and less humid conditions that continue into Saturday. 
By Saturday afternoon, a slight southwest breeze develops as the 
surface ridge settles east. A weak disturbance working into the 
region later in the day leads to fgen and some convection near a 
developing warm front, but this is favored to set up over northern 
MI so have maintained a dry forecast.

A warming trend remains on track for early next week as a 
subtropical ridge migrates from the Four Corners into the southern 
Plains and eventually the Tennessee Valley. Thickness advection 
commences Sunday, pushing temps above average, then strengthening 
southwest flow north of the ridge advects 850mb temps around 20C or 
above for Monday and Tuesday. NBM and LREF ensemble guidance 
continue to advertise 25-50% probability for highs in excess of 90 
degrees each day, with highest likelihood over the urban corridor. 
The caveat for the heat forecast will be potential for periodic MCS 
activity as several ridge-running shortwaves are shown in mid-level 
flow during this period. A cold front on Tuesday or Wednesday looks 
to break the heat and may bring a more focused signal for convection.

MARINE...

Post-frontal northwest winds in place today with peak gusts of 20-
25kts over the northern half of Lake Huron. Winds gradually weaken 
this evening as high pressure becomes established over the central 
Great Lakes. Said high then drifts overhead Friday into early 
Saturday maintaining lighter winds and quiet weather.

&&

.DTX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
MI...None.
Lake Huron...None.
Lake St Clair...None.
Michigan waters of Lake Erie...None.
&&

$$

AVIATION.....CB
DISCUSSION...TF
MARINE.......KDK


You can obtain your latest National Weather Service forecasts online
at www.weather.gov/detroit.
